rationale: Isaiah 61:1-3 describes an anointed messenger sent "to preach good news to the poor" and "to comfort all who mourn... to console the mourners... to give them a crown of beauty for ashes... the oil of joy for mourning" (BSB). Matthew 5:3-4 opens with the same two terms in the same order -- "the poor in spirit" and "those who mourn," each paired with a comfort/reward clause -- without a quotation formula, which is why the label is allusion rather than quotation. The connection is strengthened elsewhere in the canon by an explicit citation: Jesus later reads Isaiah 61:1-2 aloud in the Nazareth synagogue and applies it to himself (Luke 4:18-21), a separate, named citation this connection does not itself rest on. Ian Paul (Psephizo) independently notes the same pairing ("'Mourning' echoes Is 61:1-3").
